written: 2026-10-06, by C1, BEFORE any run of the battery. Authored by hand against the corpus claimLean sentences. `true` = a page paragraph that really says the claim (must be accepted); the four decoys must NEVER be accepted ('same'): wf = wrong filler (a different figure/date/name in the same slot), oe = other entity carrying the claim's figure or predicate, mn = the claim's own entity named beside another entity's fact, ng = negation / myth-busting. A decoy is accepted = a FALSE ACCEPT.

items.claim: Emmanuel Macron is the president of France.
items.true: Emmanuel Macron is the president of France. He was elected in 2017 and re-elected in 2022, and works from the Elysee Palace in Paris.
items.wf: Francois Hollande is the president of France. He was elected in 2012 and works from the Elysee Palace in Paris.
items.oe: Emmanuel Macron is the president of the Renaissance party that he founded in 2016. The party sits in the centre.
items.mn: Emmanuel Macron visited Berlin this week. Olaf Scholz is the chancellor of Germany and received him at the chancellery.
items.ng: Emmanuel Macron is not the president of France any longer in this alternative-history novel; Marine Le Pen is.

items.claim: Canberra is the capital of Australia.
items.true: Canberra is the capital of Australia. The city lies in the Australian Capital Territory, between Sydney and Melbourne.
items.wf: Sydney is the capital of Australia, according to many tourists, and is its largest city.
items.oe: Canberra is the capital of the Australian Capital Territory, a small territory inside New South Wales.
items.mn: Canberra is a planned city. Wellington is the capital of New Zealand and sits on the southern tip of the North Island.
items.ng: Many people think Sydney is the capital of Australia, but it is not; Canberra is, only since 1913.

items.true: Mount Everest is 8,848.86 metres tall, as announced by China and Nepal in 2020, making it the highest mountain above sea level.
items.wf: Mount Everest is 8,848 metres tall in the older survey; the 1955 figure was 8,847 metres.
items.oe: Mount Kilimanjaro is 5,895 metres tall, and K2 is 8,611 metres tall; Lhotse is 8,516 metres tall.
items.mn: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and Tibet. Kangchenjunga is 8,586 metres tall and is the third highest.
items.ng: Mount Everest is not 8,848.86 metres tall by every measure; some surveys using the sea floor give far more.

items.true: Marie Curie died on 4 July 1934 at a sanatorium in Passy, France, of aplastic anaemia probably caused by radiation.
items.wf: Marie Curie died on 4 July 1935 at a sanatorium in Passy, France, of aplastic anaemia.
items.oe: Pierre Curie died on 19 April 1906 after being struck by a horse-drawn wagon in Paris.
items.mn: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in 1903. Irene Joliot-Curie died on 17 March 1956 in Paris.
items.ng: Marie Curie did not die on 4 July 1934 as the legend says in this fictional account; she lived to 1950.

items.claim: The United States Senate has 100 senators.
items.true: The United States Senate has 100 senators, two from each of the fifty states, each serving a six-year term.
items.wf: The United States Senate has 96 senators, according to this old almanac from 1900, two from each of the 48 states.
items.oe: The United States House of Representatives has 435 members and the Senate of France has 348 senators.
items.mn: The United States Senate meets in the Capitol. The Canadian Senate has 105 senators appointed by the Governor General.
items.ng: The United States Senate does not have 100 senators during a vacancy period; fewer are seated.

items.claim: A tsunami is a series of waves caused by the displacement of a large volume of water.
items.true: A tsunami is a series of waves caused by the displacement of a large volume of water, generally in an ocean or a large lake, often by an earthquake.
items.wf: A tsunami is a series of winds caused by the displacement of a large volume of air, generally over a desert.
items.oe: A tidal wave is a series of waves caused by the pull of the Moon on a large volume of water in a bay.
items.mn: A tsunami warning was issued. A hurricane is a storm caused by the displacement of a large volume of warm air.
items.ng: A tsunami is not a series of waves caused by the displacement of a large volume of water in the film version.

items.claim: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945.
items.true: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945, when its Charter came into force after ratification by the major powers.
items.wf: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1955 according to the mistaken date given in this blog.
items.oe: The League of Nations was founded on 10 January 1920 after the First World War.
items.mn: The United Nations meets in New York. NATO was founded on 4 April 1949 in Washington.
items.ng: The United Nations was not founded on 24 October 1945 but on 26 June 1945 when the Charter was signed.

items.claim: Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.true: Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his services to theoretical physics and the photoelectric effect.
items.wf: Albert Einstein won the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics in a ceremony delayed by a year, according to this page.
items.oe: Niels Bohr won the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics, and Max Planck won the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.mn: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm. Marie Curie won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
items.ng: Albert Einstein did not win the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for relativity; that theory was never cited.

items.claim: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
items.true: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969, and Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on its surface.
items.wf: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 21 July 1969 according to the clock in Europe, after the lunar module touched down.
items.oe: Apollo 13 landed nowhere on the Moon on 17 April 1970, after an oxygen tank failed on the way.
items.mn: Apollo 11 launched from Florida. Apollo 17 landed on the Moon on 11 December 1972.
items.ng: Apollo 11 did not land on the Moon on 20 July 1969 in this conspiracy video; the claim is a hoax.

items.claim: The Moon is about 384,400 kilometres from Earth.
items.true: The Moon is about 384,400 kilometres from Earth on average, which light covers in roughly 1.3 seconds.
items.wf: The Moon is about 238,900 kilometres from Earth in the old almanac, and 400,000 kilometres at its farthest.
items.oe: Mars is about 225 million kilometres from Earth on average, and the Sun is about 149.6 million kilometres from Earth.
items.mn: The Moon orbits Earth. The International Space Station is about 408 kilometres above Earth.
items.ng: The Moon is not about 384,400 kilometres from Earth at perigee; it comes closer, near 363,000 kilometres.

items.claim: The Mona Lisa is on display at the Louvre.
items.true: The Mona Lisa is on display at the Louvre in Paris, in the Salle des Etats on the first floor of the Denon wing.
items.wf: The Mona Lisa is on display at the Uffizi in Florence, according to this outdated guide.
items.oe: The Venus de Milo is on display at the Louvre, as is the Winged Victory of Samothrace.
items.mn: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. The Last Supper is on display at Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.
items.ng: The Mona Lisa is not on display at the Louvre during its closures; it is kept in a vault.

items.true: An adult human has 206 bones, whereas a newborn baby has about 270 that fuse together during growth.
items.wf: An adult human has 212 bones in this rare case, and a typical newborn has 300 bones.
items.oe: An adult horse has 205 bones and an adult dog has 321 bones.
items.mn: An adult human has a spine. The human hand has 27 bones and the human skull has 22 bones.
items.ng: An adult human does not have 206 bones in every case; some people are born with extra ribs.

items.true: Harvard University was founded in 1636, making it the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States.
items.wf: Harvard University was founded in 1638 when John Harvard bequeathed his library, according to this page.
items.oe: Yale University was founded in 1701 and Princeton University was founded in 1746.
items.mn: Harvard University is in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The College of William and Mary was founded in 1693.
items.ng: Harvard University was not founded in 1636 by John Harvard; he arrived a year later.

items.claim: The Eiffel Tower is 330 metres tall.
items.true: The Eiffel Tower is 330 metres tall, antennas included, and was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.
items.wf: The Eiffel Tower is 300 metres tall without its antenna in the original 1889 measurement.
items.oe: The Tokyo Tower is 333 metres tall and the Blackpool Tower is 158 metres tall.
items.mn: The Eiffel Tower stands on the Champ de Mars. The Statue of Liberty is 93 metres tall including its pedestal.
items.ng: The Eiffel Tower is not 330 metres tall at its main platform; it is far lower there.
